facts.fact: The Cambridge Dictionary defines the noun 'state' (sense: condition) as a condition or way of being that exists at a particular time.
facts.quote: a [condition](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/condition "condition") or way of being that [exists]

facts.fact: The Cambridge Dictionary defines the idiom 'the state of play' (UK) as the present situation.
This Cambridge Dictionary entry for the verb 'state' is labeled with the CEFR vocabulary level B2.

Cambridge Dictionary defines 'state events' as formal, official ceremonies that involve a leader of a country or someone who represents the government, giving the state opening of Parliament and a state funeral as examples.

Cambridge Dictionary defines the sense of 'state' referring to a part of a large country that has its own government, with examples such as a state sales tax and the state superintendent of education for Indiana.
The Cambridge dictionary gives 'New York State' and 'the State of Arizona' as examples of the political units that some countries, such as the US, are divided into.
facts.quote:
New York State

the State of Arizona

facts.fact: The Cambridge dictionary states that 'the States' is another way of referring to the United States.
facts.quote: The States is another way of referring to the [United](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/united-church-of-canada "United") States:
